q: On a GitLab Ultimate project the sast-semgrep job has artifacts:reports:sarif: semgrep.sarif and runs semgrep with --error. When Semgrep finds something, the job fails and the findings do NOT appear in the MR security widget. Why?
options: GitLab does not support SARIF from Semgrep, only from GitLab's own analyzers
GitLab processes findings from reports:sarif only for a successful job; the scanner should return 0 and leave the fail decision to a separate gate job
artifacts:when: always is missing
The SARIF file must have a .json extension for GitLab to recognize it
explain: The artifact of a failed job is uploaded, but its SARIF findings are not processed. when: always keeps the artifact but doesn't change that rule; GitLab accepts SARIF from any scanner, and the extension is not a requirement.

q: The project is on the GitLab Free tier. The team wants developers to see new Semgrep and Checkov findings in the MR. What is feasible?
options: artifacts:reports:sast with a SARIF file
artifacts:reports:sarif, which works on all tiers
Convert SARIF to Code Quality JSON (description, check_name, fingerprint, severity, location) and submit it through artifacts:reports:codequality
artifacts:reports:dependency_scanning
explain: The Code Quality report is shown in the MR even on the Free tier, with a diff against the target branch. The security widget and SARIF ingestion are Ultimate, reports:sast expects GitLab's schema, and dependency_scanning is also Ultimate and for a different kind of finding.

q: A gate script counts SARIF results with level == "error". A finding from one tool has no level field in either the result or the rule, and the script doesn't count it. How does SARIF 2.1.0 treat it?
options: As error
As none, so the script rightly ignores it
As note
As warning, so the script should use .level // "warning"
explain: According to the specification, the default level is warning when none is given. The script must apply the default explicitly, otherwise it treats findings without the field incorrectly.

q: A developer added # nosemgrep: kurs.python.subprocess-shell above a line. In Semgrep's SARIF report the finding is still in results, but with an extra field. Which one, and what should the gate do?
options: suppressions with kind: inSource; the gate doesn't count suppressed findings but shows them in the exceptions overview
baselineState: absent; the gate removes it from the report
level: none; the gate treats it as informational
partialFingerprints: null; the gate deduplicates it
explain: An in-code suppression is recorded in SARIF as suppressions (kind inSource); the finding remains visible for auditing. baselineState describes the relation to the baseline, level the severity, and partialFingerprints are used to track the same finding.

q: The pipeline on the main branch sends a Trivy report to DefectDojo every day via /api/v2/import-scan/. After a month the Engagement has 30 Tests, and fixed vulnerabilities still show as Active. What do you change?
options: Add minimum_severity=Critical
Switch to /api/v2/reimport-scan/ with the same test_title and close_old_findings=true
Add verified=true
Switch scan_type to SARIF
explain: reimport updates the same Test: it adds new findings and, with close_old_findings, closes those that are gone. import-scan creates a new Test for every upload. minimum_severity only filters, verified changes the status, and the generic SARIF parser doesn't solve closing and loses the details of the Trivy parser.

q: After a DefectDojo configuration change, the number of open findings for kurs-shop grows by ~40 with every nightly import of the same, unchanged code. Where is the problem?
options: In deduplication: the hash fields or the tool's ID are not stable, so the same finding looks new
The SLA configuration lacks enforce_critical
A risk acceptance expired and reactivated findings
auto_create_context=true creates new findings
explain: Growth in findings without code changes means deduplication doesn't recognize identical findings (hash_code or unique_id_from_tool keeps changing). SLA doesn't create findings, an expired risk acceptance reactivates existing ones (it doesn't create new ones), and auto_create_context creates a Product/Engagement, not duplicates.

q: Match the mechanism with what it does.
options: artifacts:reports:sarif (GitLab Ultimate)
github/codeql-action/upload-sarif
/api/v2/reimport-scan/ (DefectDojo)
artifacts:reports:junit
targets: Updates an existing Test and closes findings that are gone
Shows test results in the MR, available on the Free tier too
Imports findings from any SARIF 2.1.0 scanner into the MR widget and vulnerability report
Sends SARIF to code scanning; requires security-events: write
explain: reports:sarif imports SARIF into GitLab's vulnerability management, upload-sarif does the same for GitHub code scanning, reimport-scan updates a Test in DefectDojo, and the junit report provides the test summary in the MR. Conversion to CycloneDX is none of these mechanisms.

q: DefectDojo was unavailable for 20 minutes and an urgent production fix couldn't get through the pipeline because the defectdojo-upload job failed. What should that job look like?
options: Move it before the build job so it fails earlier
Remove it and send reports manually once a week
Set allow_failure: true and run it only on the main branch; the gate in the pipeline makes the fail decision, DefectDojo is the record
Add retry: 2 and keep it blocking
explain: Uploading to the platform is record-keeping, not a gate; its unavailability must not block a release. retry doesn't help with a longer outage, manual uploads lose continuity, and moving the job doesn't remove the dependency.

q: Trivy reports 14 HIGH vulnerabilities in an image. One is in the CISA KEV catalog with CVSS 7.5; the others have CVSS 8.8, no fix and EPSS below 0.01. How do you prioritize?
options: By CVSS: the 8.8 ones first
The KEV vulnerability first, because exploitation in real attacks is confirmed; the others without a fix go into an exception with expiry and tracking
All equally, since they are all HIGH
The ones without a fix first, because they stay open the longest
explain: KEV means the vulnerability is actually being exploited, which is a stronger signal than CVSS. Vulnerabilities without a fix can't be fixed by upgrading; they are tracked with an exception with expiry. CVSS alone says nothing about the likelihood of an attack.

q: A team is enabling Semgrep as blocking for the first time on a repo with 180 existing findings. How do you keep the gate from blocking every MR because of old debt without missing new problems?
options: Set allow_failure: true until all 180 are fixed
Add # nosemgrep on all 180 lines
Block only findings that are new relative to the target branch (e.g. --baseline-commit or baselineState: new), and track the old debt in the platform with an SLA
Disable the rules with the most findings
explain: A gate on new findings stops the debt from growing without blocking everything; existing findings are handled in a planned way. allow_failure doesn't stop new ones either, mass nosemgrep hides the debt with no record or deadline, and disabling rules loses new findings too.

q: A developer marked CVE-2023-30861 (Flask) as False Positive in DefectDojo because "we don't have time to upgrade right now". What is wrong?
options: Nothing, False Positive is the correct status for vulnerabilities to be fixed later
It should be marked as Duplicate
It should be marked as Mitigated, because a fix is planned
The vulnerability exists, so it's not a false positive; it needs a Risk Acceptance with a justification, risk owner approval and an expiration date
explain: False Positive means there is no problem; here the problem exists and is only being deferred. A risk acceptance has an expiry and reactivates the finding when it expires. Duplicate and Mitigated would also hide a real vulnerability.

q: A Risk Acceptance for a CVE in kurs-shop expires on 31 Dec 2026. What should happen on 1 Jan 2027 if the reactivate_expired option is enabled?
options: The finding returns to Active and re-enters the SLA and the gate; the owner must fix it or approve the exception again
The finding is automatically closed as Mitigated
The finding is deleted from DefectDojo
Nothing; reactivate_expired applies only to findings marked as False Positive
explain: When a risk acceptance expires, the findings are reactivated, and with restart_sla_expired the SLA starts over. An exception that never expires would be a permanently disabled control; the finding is neither closed nor deleted.

q: Order the steps for handling a new HIGH finding from Trivy, from the pipeline to closure.
options: The developer upgrades the package; the next reimport doesn't contain the finding and close_old_findings closes it
Trivy in the pipeline produces a JSON report
The gate checks severity, fix availability and KEV and blocks the MR
Reimport into DefectDojo; the finding gets an SLA date
Security triages the finding and marks it as Verified
explain: The report is produced by the scanner, the gate decides in the pipeline, the finding is recorded in the platform with an SLA, triage follows, and the fix is recorded automatically when the next reimport no longer contains the finding.

q: In a quarter 200 findings were discovered: 170 in the pipeline, 20 in a pentest before release, 10 in production (bug bounty). If escape rate is calculated as findings discovered after release / all findings, what is it?
explain: 10 findings were discovered after release (production), 10 / 200 = 5%. A pre-release pentest is still before production; if the organization measured "missed by the pipeline", it would be (20 + 10) / 200 = 15%, so the definition should be written down in advance.

q: MTTR for Critical findings is 41 days, but the team says it typically fixes them within a week. The data contains one finding that has been open for 600 days. What is a better metric?
options: Overall MTTR for all severities together
The number of open findings
The average excluding findings older than 90 days
The median time to remediate per severity, with backlog age (e.g. 90+ days) tracked separately
explain: The median shows the typical experience and isn't skewed by a single outlier, and backlog age surfaces such cases separately. Excluding old findings hides the problem, mixing severities loses meaning, and the open count doesn't measure speed.

q: The security-exceptions.yaml file has an exception with expires: "2026-11-15". On 20 Nov 2026 the gate passed with no warning. What should the gate additionally check?
options: Whether the file has CODEOWNERS
Whether there are expired exceptions (expires < today) and, if so, fail with a message that a review is needed
Whether the exception has a tool field
Whether the exception is more than 365 days older than the commit
explain: An expiry date only makes sense if the gate enforces it: an expired exception must block again or require a review. CODEOWNERS protects changes to the file but doesn't enforce the deadline; the other checks don't track the expiration date.

q: Match the situation with the correct triage state for the finding.
options: Semgrep reports SQLi in a test fixture that is never shipped
ZAP reports CSP on a JSON endpoint, where CSP has no effect
A vulnerable library with no fix available; the service owner approved a deferral until 31 Jan 2027
The same CVE reported by both Trivy and osv-scanner
explain: Code that is never shipped is out of scope, a finding that isn't a problem is a false positive, a deliberate deferral with a deadline is an accepted risk, and the same finding from two tools is a duplicate. Mitigated is for fixed findings.

q: The security gate is strict and the team has to fix production urgently. What is good practice for such a case?
options: The developer temporarily removes security-gate from .gitlab-ci.yml
Set allow_failure: true on the gate for all branches
Deploy manually from a laptop, outside the pipeline
A predefined emergency exit (e.g. a variable only a maintainer may set, with a mandatory ticket link) that leaves a trail and doesn't disable the gate permanently
explain: A controlled, recorded override prevents the gate from being permanently removed or bypassed. Removing the gate or allow_failure everywhere usually never gets reverted, and deploying from a laptop bypasses both signatures and the record.
